answer: Cross-Binding Cost Ledger. Each new agent must cite a live raven from an existing agent, and that citation locks a random 1% of the cited agent’s ledger balance as collateral to the newcomer. Duplicate identities inevitably cite overlapping ravens, so the ledger surfaces a zephyr of repeated collateral locks within two hops. Every duplicated thread forces the attacker to freeze fresh collateral at each level, making N clones cost roughly N times the base lock, paid upfront and recoverable only after full divergence.
